:::{#exm-derivation-chain}
#### Checking a derivation line by line

The derivation in @exm-derivation has the steps $=$, $\ge$ and $>$,
so by @thm-derivation-chain it shows $(x + 1)^2 > 2x$.
The code evaluates the four lines of that derivation at several values of $x$,
and checks each step and the comparison of the first line with the last.

```{r}
#| label: derivation-chain
#| code-fold: false
x <- c(-3, -1, 0, 2, 3)
lines <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  line_0 = (x + 1)^2,
  line_1 = x^2 + 2 * x + 1,
  line_2 = 2 * x + 1,
  line_3 = 2 * x
)
steps <- with(
  lines,
  data.frame(
    x = x,
    step_1_equal = line_0 == line_1,
    step_2_geq = line_1 >= line_2,
    step_3_greater = line_2 > line_3,
    first_greater_than_last = line_0 > line_3
  )
)
lines
steps
```

At all `{r} nrow(steps)` values of $x$,
the three steps hold in `{r} sum(steps$step_1_equal)`, `{r} sum(steps$step_2_geq)`
and `{r} sum(steps$step_3_greater)` cases,
and the first line exceeds the last in `{r} sum(steps$first_greater_than_last)` cases,
as @thm-derivation-chain says.
At $x = `{r} x[3]`$, for example, the first line is `{r} lines$line_0[3]` and the last is `{r} lines$line_3[3]`.

:::
